note.text: A formal speech addresses a stated audience and occasion. Its opening identifies the purpose, its body develops reasons and its ending makes the next step clear. Suitable wording matters more than unnecessary complexity. Preserve a source’s uncertainty: a proposal is not a success already achieved. The original model is not a universal examination template. Live delivery and audience response require separate practice.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text: By the end, you should be able to adapt concerns into a formally addressed speech with a supported request. Builds on: directed-writing choices and reading proposals. Leads to: a less formal talk and reported viewpoints.

sections.heading: Read the original model
sections.text: Original model extract: Chairperson, teachers and fellow pupils, thank you for the opportunity to speak. I ask the club to consider a noticeboard for checked opportunities. paper_task.prompt: Write a formal speech requesting a supervised noticeboard pilot. Address the school audience, explain the obstacle, develop a reason, acknowledge a limit and end with a request. Rehearse delivery separately.
model: Chairperson, teachers and fellow pupils, thank you for the opportunity to speak. I ask the club to consider a noticeboard for checked opportunities. Our fictional source describes members who hear about vacancies after the deadline. That information problem deserves a practical response.

A useful noticeboard would identify the source and closing date of each notice. Volunteers could check whether old notices should be removed. This would help readers verify information, although it would not guarantee selection or create every opportunity they need.

I request permission for a supervised pilot and a review of whether pupils can understand and check the notices. Let us begin with a clear responsibility rather than an unsupported promise. Thank you.
checklist: Formal address: an opening recognising the stated audience.
Supported purpose: a request connected to relevant information.
Qualified claim: a benefit stated without an unsupported guarantee.
Closing request: a clear next step at the speech’s end.
Use relevant original details and check sentence boundaries, agreement and spelling.
